eyebrow: Lesson 17 · B1 · Good Manners with Family · 20 câu
heading: Asking Nicely at Home
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Manners with Family – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 4–7.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Manners with Family (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Home is where you feel most {comfortable|comfortable}. You are with the people who know you best: your family! They see your messy hair in the morning, they hear you singing in the shower and, sometimes, they even smell your {stinky|stinky} socks.

paras.label: B
paras.text: So do you still need good manners at home? Absolutely. Your family lives in the same space and shares many rooms and things. Good manners show {respect|respect}, and they help keep everyone happy {under one roof|under one roof}.

paras.label: C
paras.text: If you want something, ask for it nicely, using polite words like "Please" and "May I". Say "Please pass the chicken" instead of "Give me the chicken." Ask politely and you will probably get what you want. Be {rude|rude}, and the chicken might {end up|end up} in your lap!

paras.label: D
paras.text: Saying "Thank you" matters too. If your brother helps you with your homework, thank him. It shows that you {appreciate|appreciate} your family, and he will be happy to help again. With his help, you might even get top marks in your next maths test!

paras.label: E
paras.text: In India, children show respect to older {relatives|relatives} in a special way: they {bow down|bow down} and touch the relative's feet. Customs are different around the world, but the idea behind them is the same: we should {treat|treat} our families with care.

parts.title: Part 1 · Matching headings
parts.instr: Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Mỗi tiêu đề dùng một lần.
options: Why manners still matter at home

items.label: Paragraph A
items.why: Đoạn A: ở nhà, gia đình thấy con người thật của bạn.

items.label: Paragraph B
items.why: Đoạn B: *So do you still need good manners at home? Absolutely.*

items.label: Paragraph C
items.why: Đoạn C: dùng *Please*, *May I* khi muốn xin gì.

items.label: Paragraph D
items.why: Đoạn D: cảm ơn anh trai giúp làm bài.

items.label: Paragraph E
items.why: Đoạn E: phong tục ở Ấn Độ.

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: In (A), why does the writer mention messy hair, singing and stinky socks?
options: to show that your family sees you as you really are
to explain how to look tidy
to complain about brothers and sisters
to give advice on washing clothes
questions.why: Những chi tiết đời thường → gia đình biết rõ bạn nhất.

questions.q: The writer believes good manners are only necessary outside the home.
questions.why: Sai. *So do you still need good manners at home? Absolutely.*

questions.q: Which request is the most polite, according to (C)?
questions.why: *Say "Please pass the chicken" instead of "Give me the chicken."*

questions.q: *Be rude, and the chicken might end up in your lap!* What does the writer mean?
options: Rude requests may not get you what you want.
You should eat on the sofa.
Your family will give you extra food.
questions.why: Câu đùa: hỏi thô lỗ thì không được như ý.

questions.q: According to (D), thanking your brother makes him more likely to help you again.
questions.why: Đúng. *he will be happy to help again.*

questions.q: How do children in India show respect to older relatives?
options: They bow down and touch their feet.
questions.why: *they bow down and touch the relative's feet.*

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: Which detail from (A) does this picture show?
options: Your family sometimes smells your stinky socks.
Your family hears you sing in the shower.
Your family sees your messy hair.
Your family helps with your homework.
questions.why: Cô bé bịt mũi vì mùi tất → *smell your stinky socks*.
questions.alt: A man relaxes in an armchair reading a newspaper with his socked feet on a stool, while a girl holds her nose because of the smell

questions.q: Which polite word does the girl use?
questions.why: *Please pass…* – đúng lời khuyên ở đoạn C.
questions.alt: Two girls sit at the dinner table; one smiles and says: Please pass the biscuits.

questions.q: Which paragraph gives the advice that this girl is following?
questions.why: Đoạn C: hỏi xin một cách lịch sự.
questions.alt: Two girls sit at the dinner table; one smiles and says: Please pass the biscuits.

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Last week I was stuck on my maths homework. [1] He sat with me for half an hour and explained everything step by step. [2] The next day, I got nine out of ten in the test. [3]
options: So I asked my older brother, "Could you help me, please?"
My brother shouted, "Give me your pencil!" and walked away.
When we finished, I gave him a hug and said, "Thanks so much!"
My brother was so pleased that he offered to help me again next week.
I decided to go to bed without finishing it.

items.why: Cần một *He* đã được nhắc trước đó → người anh.
Lời cảm ơn khiến anh sẵn lòng giúp tiếp (ý đoạn D).

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *…keep everyone happy under one roof* (B). **Under one roof** means…
questions.why: **Under one roof** = sống chung một nhà.

questions.q: *…the chicken might end up in your lap* (C). To **end up** somewhere means to…
questions.why: **End up** = rốt cuộc lại ở đâu đó.

questions.q: *Home is where you feel most comfortable* (A). **Comfortable** here means…
